senses.gloss: (cmp. מָחָה) [to blot out, annul,] to remit (a debt); to forgive, pardon, to forego, renounce.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 85b:9">Keth. 85ᵇ</cite> <he>המוכר … וחזר ומְחָלוֹ מָחוּל</he> if one sells a note of indebtedness to a neighbor, and then remits the debt, it stands remitted (and the buyer of the note must settle with the creditor).
<cite ref="Ketubot 85b">Ib.</cite> <he>מְחָלַתּוּ</he> she remitted it. Y. B. Mets. VI, end, 11ᵃ <he>שמָחֲלוּ להם מוכסין</he> to whom custom officers remitted the fine.
<cite ref="Yoma 2a">Ib.</cite> <he>לשם פלוני מָחַלְנוּ</he> we remitted (the fine) for this man’s sake (individually).
<cite ref="Berakhot 12b:9">Ber. 12ᵇ</cite> <he>מוֹחֲלִין לו על כל וכ׳</he> all his sins are forgiven to him.
<cite ref="Berakhot 32a:9-16">Ib. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>איני</he> … <he>עד שתִּמְחוֹל ותסלח להם וכ׳</he> I will not leave thee until thou forgivest and pardonest &c.—
Sabb. 30ᵃ מְחוֹל לי על וכ׳ forgive me that particular sin (the seduction of Bathsheba); מָחוּל לך thou art forgiven; a. v. fr.—מ׳ על כבודו to forego the honor due to one’s self.

<cite ref="Kiddushin 32a:15">Kidd. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>האב שמ׳ … כבודו מָחוּל</he> if a father allows a son to omit the acts of reverence due to him, his honor is remitted (the son may avail himself of the permission); <he>הרב שמ׳ וכ׳</he> but if a teacher gives permission &c.; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 19:23">Num. R. s. 19</cite> <he>שאין המוֹחֵל נעשה וכ׳</he> for he who is asked to forgive, must not be relentless (v.

senses.gloss: to be cancelled; to be forgiven, pardoned.
units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 17a">B. Mets. 17ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Gittin 26b">Gitt. 26ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>שטר … שכבר נ׳ שעבודו</he> on a note once given and paid off you cannot raise a loan again, because the security which it contains (v. <cite ref="A01052"><he>אַחֲרָיוּת</he></cite>) has once been cancelled.
<cite ref="Yoma 88a:10">Yoma 88ᵃ</cite> <he>סדורין לִימָּחֵל</he> (his sins) lie ready to be forgiven.
<cite ref="Taanit 7b:3">Taan. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>אא״כ נִמְחֲלוּ וכ׳</he> unless Israel’s sins are forgiven.

<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 8:7">B. Kam. VIII, 7</cite> <he>אע״פ שהוא נותן אין נ׳ לו וכ׳</he> although he pays (the fine for insulting a neighbor), he is not forgiven (by the Lord), until he asks pardon; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="M00869"><he>מְחִילָה</he></cite>.
